title: fix(app-shell,plugin-chatbot,i18n): AI build surface UX — land on the running app, a task-named composer, one usage meter, a gauge that is not a spinner, a localized scope chip (objectui#11658)
body:
Fixes #11658

This fixes the five AI build surface items from the 2026-10-05 cloud acceptance run (the objectui half of cloud#2627, cloud#2634 and cloud#2435 item 8). Each item can be accepted on its own. The rulings on the card were applied as written.

## What changed, per item

1. **After the first AI build, the user lands on the running app.**
   - The post-build jump starts in objectui, not in cloud. ChatPane's built-moment transition navigates to `/studio/PKG/interfaces`. The `?surface=dashboard:NAME` part is added afterwards by the Interfaces pillar's `useSurfaceDeepLink` mirror when it auto-opens the first nav leaf. The cloud build envelope supplies only the package id.
   - The transition now passes router state, `STUDIO_RUN_LANDING` from the new `studioLanding.ts`. The Interfaces pillar reads it once, at mount. It opens the canvas in **运行 / Run** with the properties aside collapsed.
   - The first click on **设计 / Design** brings back the design overlays and the aside that the landing collapsed. If the user collapses or expands the aside themselves, the landing no longer controls it.
   - Every other arrival opens in Design with the aside open, as before. That includes the explicit "Design in Studio" door and any reload or shared link, because router state does not travel in the URL (Commandment #8: this is a one-shot arrival intent, not addressable state).
2. **The in-app composer names the task.** When ChatPane runs the build agent scoped to a package (`editPackageId`), the placeholder is `console.ai.askOrChangeApp`. In zh it reads 「问问数据，或让我改改这个应用…」 and in en "Ask about your data, or ask me to change this app…". This applies to the console dock in a running app, the Studio dock and `/ai/build?package=`. The cold-start build surface and the ask agent keep their placeholders.
3. **The usage popover shows one meter.**
   - The popover shows the pool's used share as a single percentage, `console.ai.usage.poolUsed` (for example "19% used").
   - The build / data-Q&A split is no longer drawn. Its keys `meterBuild`, `meterAsk` and `breakdownTitle` are removed from all ten packs.
   - `useAiUsage` still reads `breakdown` strictly from the wire. Nothing renders it any more (see Acceptance notes).
4. **The usage ring no longer looks like a spinner.** The glyph (`MeterGauge`, which replaces `MeterRing`) is a closed outline in the tone colour around a pie wedge that fills clockwise from 12 o'clock. Before, it was a stroked arc over a faint 25%-opacity track. At low usage that drew a short open arc, which is the outline of a spinner. A pie inside a closed outline reads as a quantity at any fraction.
5. **The plan card's scope chip is localized and shows the app's label.**
   - Both chip sites now read the pack sentence `chatbot.plan.extendTarget` instead of the English default "Adding to existing app". The two sites are the proposed-plan card and `BlueprintProgressPanel`, and they share one `useExtendChip` hook.
   - The chip names the target app by the label the host resolves. The new optional `resolveAppLabel` prop on `ChatbotEnhanced` does this, and ChatPane passes one built from the metadata apps. The machine name moves to the chip's tooltip.
   - A host `planExtendLabel` still takes precedence.

## Mechanism assumptions (from the dispatch)

- **B1 verified.** The navigation is decided inside objectui, in the built-moment effect in `AiChatPage.tsx`, the one that calls `paneNavigate`. The cloud side does not need to change.
- **B2 partly falsified.** `console.ai.askAgent` is read at **one** source site, ChatPane's `placeholder` prop. ChatPane has **three** hosts: the full-page `AiChatPage`, the console `ChatDock` (`ChatDockConversation`), and the Studio dock (`StudioAiCopilot`). Fixing that one site covers all of them.
- **B3 verified.** The literal appeared twice in code in `ChatbotEnhanced`: the `planExtendLabel` default and the `BlueprintProgressPanel` `extendLabel` default. A third occurrence was in a JSDoc. All three are gone.

## Verification (at the head this PR was opened on)

- New tests:
  - `StudioDesignSurface.runLanding-11658.test.tsx` (item 1, pillar)
  - `AiChatPage.builtLandsRunning-11658.test.tsx` (item 1, producer, with the "Design in Studio" door as the control)
  - `AiChatPage.appContextComposer-11658.test.tsx` (item 2, plus the host half of item 5)
  - The rewritten `AiUsageIndicator.test.tsx` blocks "the popover figure (one meter)" (item 3) and "the gauge glyph (not a spinner)" (item 4)
  - `ChatbotEnhanced.extendChip-11658.test.tsx` (item 5). This pins that the zh chip contains **no ASCII-only literal**: it has no Latin-letter run at all, and the target label in the fixture is Chinese.
- Ablation: for each one, only the source was mutated, the mutation was proven to be on disk by counting the marker, the tests went red, then the file was restored with `git checkout HEAD`. The restore was proven by the on-disk blob hash equalling the HEAD blob and by an empty `git diff HEAD`, and the tests went green again.
  - Item 1 (pillar ignores the state): 2 red → restored 5/5 green.
  - Item 1 (Design does not hand the aside back): 1 red → restored 5/5 green.
  - Item 1 (producer navigates without the state): 2 red → restored 3/3 green.
  - Item 2 (no app-context branch): 2 red → restored 5/5 green.
  - Item 3 (indicator reverted to the base file): 2 red → restored 2/2 green.
  - Item 4 (same revert): 3 red → restored 3/3 green.
  - Item 5 (the chip goes back to an English template literal): 4 red → restored 6/6 green.
- Gates, all with exit 0 unless noted:
  - `type-check` for `@object-ui/i18n`, `@object-ui/plugin-chatbot` and `@object-ui/app-shell`, after `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...'`.
  - The test suites for `packages/plugin-chatbot/` and `packages/i18n/`, and `packages/app-shell/` (results are in the report comment).
  - `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:i18n-dead-keys`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new citations), `changeset:check`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, and `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`.
- Lint: a narrowed run of `eslint --no-inline-config` over the 20 changed `.ts`/`.tsx` files. Its one error, `react-hooks/static-components` in the DataPillar header, already exists on the base file and is suppressed inline in normal runs. Linting each of the four touched source files at base and at head gives identical per-rule counts. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI.
- **NOT VERIFIED IN BROWSER**, for all five items. The console has no cheap mock mode for the AI build surface or for the cloud usage endpoint, and the dispatch rules out booting a cloud stack. The epic's final re-walk covers it, including the URL the build lands on: `/studio/PKG/interfaces?surface=dashboard:NAME`, now in Run.

## Acceptance notes

- **File surface.** Item 1's landing half lives in `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/` (`StudioDesignSurface.tsx`, the new `studioLanding.ts` and its test). That is outside the claim's listed globs. I took it as "the post-build navigation site it finds", because the dispatch asks for the objectui half of the default tab and the collapsed panel, and both are state of the Interfaces pillar.
- **Out of scope.** The cold-start build surface (no package) still reads "Ask Build…" / 「向 构建 提问…」. The ruling scopes item 2 to the in-app context, and "change this app" would be wrong with no app. This is not filed. If the maintainer wants it, it is a one-line follow-up at the same placeholder site.
- **Dormant read.** `useAiUsage` still parses `breakdown` strictly, and no renderer reads it now. The wire contract was left alone. If cloud drops the field, its parser test is the place to retire it. No one owns that follow-up.
